chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Ibn Abi Nasr, from Aban, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): Is it permissible to exchange one qafiz of wheat for two qafizs of barley? He said: 'It is not permissible except like for like.' Then he said: 'For barley is from wheat [in kind/category].'

key_terms.قَفِيزٌ: A traditional unit of volume measurement for dry goods
key_terms.مِثْلًا بِمِثْلٍ: Like for like (equal quantity and quality)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on exchanging wheat for barley in unequal amounts according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) rules that exchanging one qafiz of wheat for two qafizs of barley is impermissible, establishing the principle of 'mithlan bi-mithl' (equal for equal). He clarifies that although barley is a type of grain, it is distinct from wheat in this context, preventing unequal exchange (riba al-fadl) between these specific commodities. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on precise commodity classification to avoid usury in spot transactions.
